title: Rung A: check_schema enforces minLength and minItems over 422 already-declared sites
objective: Switch on the walker over declarations that already exist. `minLength` (377 declarations across 49 schema files) and `minItems` (48 across 32) are declared throughout the corpus and enforced nowhere: check_schema implements exactly seven keywords, established by AST enumeration over the function rather than by testing a candidate list. This rung adds two branches and re-points the tests that were compensating for their absence.
business_value: A `minLength: 1` on a governance field reads as a guarantee that the field is non-empty and is not one, so authors have been paying for the gap three times over -- a declaration that does nothing, a code control that does the work, and a comment explaining the difference. It has also produced incorrect governance analysis: #293 scoped itself with "12 of 13 are closed by schema minLength: 1" and those closures do not execute.
in_scope: scripts/badf_gate.py: two branches in check_schema's walker (minLength on strings, minItems on arrays) and the docstring that lists what it enforces
tests/test_badf_schema_length_bounds.py: the enforcement battery -- two depths, negative controls, and a mutation battery that neuters the rung's own branch
re-pointing the 19 tests whose probes were shadowed by the new refusal, across 7 existing test modules
CHANGELOG.md entry recording that a NEW record can now be refused where it was not before
out_of_scope: every other unimplemented keyword: const (27, Rung B), format (61), $ref (44, dangling -- #313), anyOf (7), minimum/maximum (5)
the 3 minLength/minItems sites buried inside anyOf -- unreachable without an anyOf branch, so this rung reaches 422 of 425
removing any compensating code control, even one now exactly shadowed -- criterion 5 forbids it here; disposition is deferred to its own issue
the degenerate-content class (#293): minLength is a LENGTH bound and admits '   ', so this closes the exact-empty instance and not the class
check_schema's docstring as a positive list (#315) -- the list is made accurate here, the negative enumeration is that issue's deliverable
acceptance_criteria: check_schema refuses a string shorter than its declared minLength and an array with fewer items than its declared minItems, naming path, declared bound and received value
enforcement is asserted at two depths -- a root-level array bound and a bound nested inside array items -- because a root-only implementation passes a depth-1 test
a conforming record is still admitted, asserted per bounded site, so a rule that over-refuses cannot pass the refusal tests
each new assertion is shown RED before the walker change, and neutering the rung's own source block re-admits every probe the battery refuses (SARCHI C1)

all 19 shadowed tests are re-pointed at the degenerate form only their code control catches; where no such form exists the test is recorded as SHADOWED with its control retained, never silently dropped (SARCHI C2)
no compensating code control is removed
the replay is re-run on the COMMITTED tree with the SHA cited, and the suite is reported as a diff against baseline on the same tree
the anyOf-buried sites are pinned as still-unenforced by a behavioural test, so a green suite cannot be read as full coverage
evidence: red-first run of the new battery before the walker change: 5 of 10 assertions RED, negative controls correctly green on both sides
mutation battery: the rung's source block removed verbatim from a copy, every probe re-admitted, with a positive control proving the neutered walker still works
record replay at main@310a660 with a baseline: 694 records, 292 refused with and without the rule, 0 newly refused
full suite as a diff against a green baseline on the same tree

rollback.method: revert the squash commit via PR

note: Touches ZERO paths under schemas/ -- the declarations already exist; this switches on the walker. Confirmed to SARCHI by measurement including untracked files, so #313 (which adds a $defs block and an unscoped schemas/ sweep) is disjoint and proceeds in parallel. expected_surfaces omits badf/lockfile.json deliberately: the lockfile and the record's own work/ dir are excluded from the governed diff by construction, so declaring either is refused as C7 authority attached to nothing (GOV-0108).
